prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After the full round-1 exchange I keep the same single-achievement configuration, and I do so on the science rather than on the fact that all six of us arrived at it. GLP-1 is a case where basic hormone physiology came first and the drug class followed from it: the incretin effect and the secretion of the active peptide (Holst), the identification of the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form (Mojsov), and the characterisation of its wider actions on islets, gut and central appetite circuits and the case for acting on them (Drucker). Each of the three is a distinct step that had to exist before any analogue could be designed. The clinical consequence is confirmed by several independent drugs and large randomized outcome trials, with cardiovascular and renal benefit beyond glycaemia and weight, so the maturity question is settled and recognition now is timely rather than premature. A one-part prize also keeps the citation about discovery, which I think is the clearest fit with the prize's remit.
statement.case_against: The cost of this configuration is real and I do not want it hidden: Lotte Bjerre Knudsen's long-acting analogue design is what produced the medicines patients take, and a physiology citation leaves her outside the prize. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide relative to Habener and others outside the credited list remains contested, and the supplied record does not let me resolve it; if colleagues could show her role is weaker than described, my allocation would need to be reopened. A second concern is that the strongest alternative, CAR-T limited to June and Sadelain, is equally mature and has a clear concept-to-clinic story, so a reader could fairly say the committee chose GLP-1 on salience. I have tested that and still find B041 broader in original biology and impact, but the margin is attribution-driven rather than a large scientific gap.

responses.point: You said that calling Knudsen's work merely translational understates it, because the drugs that changed care are her designs and the prize has honoured therapeutic development before, and that a physiology-centred prize should admit it leaves a real gap.
responses.response: I accept your correction and withdraw the loose wording in my round-1 reply. My reason for not displacing anyone is that the citation is then about physiology, not that drug design is lesser. If we named Knudsen we would have to argue explicitly which of Drucker, Holst or Mojsov is least central, and I cannot make that case on documented grounds: Holst's secretion and incretin physiology, Mojsov's active peptide and Drucker's biology and translational case each stand on a different step. So I keep three names, and I would want the committee record to state plainly that the exclusion is a judgment about what the discovery is, not a finding that her contribution is minor.

responses.point: You doubt that optogenetics should rise above B041 or B030 because six credited names cannot be cut to three without omitting people with serious claims, and you note that a single-achievement prize keeps the B041 citation about physiology; the chair's question also asks whether a one-part or two-part prize is preferable.
responses.response: I agree on both points and it has firmed my view. A two-part prize would force B041 down to two names, and I see no documented ground for dropping any of the physiology three, so a second part is only worth it if the case is clearly stronger than the loss. Optogenetics is not: my Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann trio still leaves out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck, and its clinical effect is early. I have also tried to discount my own field proximity. I therefore keep B039 only as a listed alternative and prefer one part for B041.

responses.point: You propose crediting only June and Sadelain for CAR-T and say you would reopen the B041 question only if the citation were centred on the therapies, arguing then about which of the three is least central instead of assuming Mojsov.
responses.response: I support the narrower B030 pairing as the only defensible form of that part, but it still does not displace B041 for me because the chimeric receptor originators such as Eshhar sit outside the credited names. I also agree with your condition on B041: if the committee chose drugs over physiology, the choice of who gives way must be argued on documented steps. Where I differ slightly is on B023. Imatinib is very mature, but it rests on earlier chromosomal and kinase biology and on industrial chemistry, so a clean three-person split is harder than for GLP-1, and I keep it out of my alternatives.

responses.point: You say waiting on B041 would cost little if the credit dispute cannot be resolved because CAR-T is equally mature, and you would give up one of the three names only if the citation were framed around the drugs and a cleaner account of Mojsov's role were available.
responses.response: I take the waiting argument seriously but I do not find it persuasive here. The unresolved item is Mojsov's priority, and nothing in our record shows that delay would resolve it, whereas B030 carries its own unresolved credit problem with Eshhar and the question of Rosenberg. Postponing B041 would therefore trade one attribution uncertainty for another. I agree that if we ever reframed B041 around the drugs, we would first need a clearer account of Mojsov's role than we hold, and I would not assume she is the name to give way.

responses.point: You rank B035 as a strong, low-risk alternative for a basic-science prize but see the link from mechanism to medicine as largely associative, and you keep B041 anchored in physiology.
responses.response: I agree with your reading of B035: Mori and Walter are a clean pairing, but the mechanism-to-medicine connection is still associative, and Ron's PERK and CHOP work sits outside the names, so I do not use it as a preferred part or alternative. On the chair's question about which criterion should decide the strongest alternative, I weigh demonstrated clinical effect together with clean attribution, which is why B030 comes before B035 for me.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, relative to Habener and others outside the credited list, is as strong as the supplied record implies; I cannot verify it and it is the point that could reopen my three-name allocation.
Whether the committee will frame the citation around physiology or around drug design, since that choice, not the science itself, decides whether Knudsen displaces one of the three.
Whether B030 limited to June and Sadelain is robust enough, given that the chimeric receptor originators are outside the credited names, if B041 were set aside.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate is apparent from my profile. I repeat the disclosures from round 1: a 2009 co-authored paper with Thomas Perlmann on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons and a past collaboration with Sten Grillner, neither of which touches a shortlisted ballot. My field of circuit neuroscience is adjacent to B039, which I keep only as an alternative and have tried not to let that proximity raise it. No new disclosure arose in round 2.
